Appendix C: Environment variables used for RPG
      There are several environment variables you can use to control the RPG compiler and the RPG runtime.

      Environment variables for troubleshooting
      Troubleshooting unexpected errors in RPG runtime service program QRNXIO
         Unexpected errors in RPG runtime service program QRNXIO are often caused by storage corruption
         in the RPG module that affects the internal data structures used by RPG to handle the files in the
         module.
         • Compile-time environment variable QIBM_RPG_CHECK_FILES causes the compiler to insert
           additional code to check the internal data structures for handling your files.
         • Runtime environment variable QIBM_RPG_CHECK_FILES_ACTION is used to control the action
           taken by the RPG runtime if the internal storage for a file is found to be corrupted.
         For more information about these environment variables, including the PTFs you need, see https://
         www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/7273537.
      Troubleshooting exceptions when calling Java methods
         If environment variable QIBM_RPG_JAVA_EXCP_TRACE environment variable is present with the
         value 'Y' when the exception occurs, a exception trace is produced.
         See the topic about getting information about exceptions thrown by called Java methods in the
         Rational Development Studio for i: ILE RPG Programmer's Guide.




1056 IBM i: ILE RPG Reference
Troubleshooting unexpected errors for DATA-GEN and DATA-INTO
   See QIBM_RPG_DATA_GEN_TRACE and QIBM_RPG_DATA_INTO_TRACE_PARSER in “Runtime
   environment variables” on page 1058.

Compile-time environment variables
The compile-time environment variables are only needed when the module or program is being compiled.
They are not needed at runtime.
QIBM_RPG_PCML_VERSION
   This environment variable can be used to control the PCML version if PGMINFO(*PCML) is in effect.
   See “PGMINFO(*PCML | *NO | *DCLCASE { : *MODULE { : *Vx }})” on page 387.
QIBM_RPG_PPSRCFILE_LENGTH
   This environment variable is used when the CRTSQLRPGI is used with RPGPPOPT(*LVL1) or
   RPGPPOPT(*LVL2). The SQL precompiler calls the RPG compiler in preprocessor mode to create
   a source member in the QTEMP/QSQLPRE source file. This source member receives the required
   source lines from the primary source plus any /COPY files and /INCLUDE files if RPGPPOPT(*LVL2)
   is specified.
   If it does not already exist, the RPG compiler creates the QTEMP/QSQLPRE source file.
   You can control the record length of the output file QTEMP/QSQLPRE created by the RPG
   preprocessor. The default record length is 112, which supports a line length up to 100. If the primary
   source or any included source is fully free, the default line length of 100 might not be long enough to
   handle all the lines for the QTEMP/QSQLPRE file.
   You can control the line length of the QTEMP/QSQLPRE file created by the RPG preprocessor in two
   ways.
   • To request that the QTEMP/QSQLPRE file be created with a specific line length, you can use
     environment variable QIBM_RPG_PPSRCFILE_LENGTH.
     For example, if you know that a line length of 500 is sufficient for all the source in the compilation,
     specify a value of 500 for the environment variable.



        ADDENVVAR QIBM_RPG_PPSRCFILE_LENGTH VALUE(500)



   • If the environment variable is not present, the PPMINOUTLN parameter for CRTBNDRPG and
     CRTRPGMOD sets the minimum line length for the output file.
     If the length of a line in the source file specified by the SRCFILE parameter or the maximum length
     of a line in the source file specified by the SRCSTMF parameter is longer than the length specified by
     the PPMINOUTLN parameter, the output file is created with the longer length.
     For example, to request that the QTEMP/QSQLPRE file be created with a line length at least 500,
     specify COMPILEOPT('PPMINOUTLN(500)'). That will cause the RPG preprocessor to create the
     output file with a line length that is at least 500, but might be longer if the longest line in the input
     file is longer than 500.



        CRTSQLRPGI MYLIB/MYPGM SRCSTMF('mypgm.sqlrpgle') RPGPPOPT(*LVL1)
        COMPILEOPT('PPMINOUTLN(500)')




                                                                                             Appendixes 1057
      QIBM_RPG_RNF7031_EVENTS
         If this environment variable is present at compile time with value 'N', the compiler will not place
         RNF7031 messages into the event file.

           ADDENVVAR QIBM_RPG_RNF7031_EVENTS VALUE('N')

         This can reduce the time needed to import the event file into an editor.
         This environment variable is only checked when OPTION(*EVENTF) is specified for the compile.

      Runtime environment variables
      The runtime environment variables are needed when the program or service program is being run. They
      are not needed at compile time.
      QIBM_RPG_DATA_GEN_TRACE
         This environment variable can be used to obtain a trace of the information passed to and from
         the program or procedure specified by the %GEN built-in function for the DATA-GEN operation. See
         “DATA-GEN (Generate a Document from a Variable)” on page 817.
      QIBM_RPG_DATA_INTO_TRACE_PARSER
         This environment variable can be used to obtain a trace of the information passed from the program or
         procedure specified by the %PARSER built-in function for the DATA-INTO operation. See “DATA-INTO
         (Parse a Document into a Variable)” on page 820.
      QIBM_RPG_JAVA_PROPERTIES
         This environment variable can be used to set the Java properties required when the RPG runtime
         starts the JVM in your job due to an RPG program or service program calling a Java method.
         See the topic about controlling how the Java Virtual Machine is set up in the Rational Development
         Studio for i: ILE RPG Programmer's Guide.

      Release-specific environment variables related to PTFs
      There are several other compile-time environment variables that are associated with PTFs. They are used
      for 2 purposes:
      • Immediately enable a fix provided by a PTF that will be enabled by default in a later release.
      • Immediately enable the compiler to issue an error for a scenario that will be disallowed by the compiler
        in a later release.
      For more information about these environment variables, including the PTFs you need, see https://
      www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/7271860.
